citation_entries.sentence: Across three centuries of on-and-off danger, property was seized, teachers' fathers were beheaded, and bishops fled.
In those years the church's whole authority was persuasion.

On wealth, Clement spoke to the rich in his sermon on who can be saved: “Consider someone who holds possessions - gold, silver, houses - as gifts of God. From them he serves the God who gives them, for the salvation of others. He knows he owns them more for the sake of his fellow believers than for his own. He is master of what he owns, not a slave to the things he owns. He does not carry them around in his soul. He does not bind his life within them or fence it in. Instead, he is always at work on some good and divine task. One day he may be forced to lose them. Even then, he can bear their loss with a cheerful mind, just as he bears their abundance. This is the one the Lord blesses, the one called poor in spirit. He is a fit heir of the kingdom of heaven, not one who could not live rich.”
After 325 the emperor called the council and the confession was enforced.
The church itself learned to use exile and condemnation, and some of what was done with that power our own sources report without pride.
Still, what the apostles delivered plainly stood fixed, and everything else was open ground.
On that ground, asking, testing and correcting was how a soul grew.

text: Before 325, belonging to us could cost property, safety and even life. Across three centuries of on-and-off danger, property was seized, teachers' fathers were beheaded, and bishops fled. In those years the church's whole authority was persuasion. On wealth, Clement spoke to the rich in his sermon on who can be saved: “Consider someone who holds possessions - gold, silver, houses - as gifts of God. From them he serves the God who gives them, for the salvation of others. He knows he owns them more for the sake of his fellow believers than for his own. He is master of what he owns, not a slave to the things he owns. He does not carry them around in his soul. He does not bind his life within them or fence it in. Instead, he is always at work on some good and divine task. One day he may be forced to lose them. Even then, he can bear their loss with a cheerful mind, just as he bears their abundance. This is the one the Lord blesses, the one called poor in spirit. He is a fit heir of the kingdom of heaven, not one who could not live rich.”. After 325 the emperor called the council and the confession was enforced. The church itself learned to use exile and condemnation, and some of what was done with that power our own sources report without pride. Still, what the apostles delivered plainly stood fixed, and everything else was open ground. On that ground, asking, testing and correcting was how a soul grew.
